calls.head: Like for like: Barron vs. Bowman
calls.body: At home, the Jets keep sending Barron’s line (Koepke, Barron and Zhilkin) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Scott Arniel keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Golden Knights’ fourth line is Gatcomb, Dowd and Bowman.

calls.body: The Golden Knights’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Jets’ kill is near the bottom. The Jets need to stay out of the box.

calls.head: The Golden Knights should drive the play
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Golden Knights have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Jets near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Golden Knights’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

surprises.head: Winnipeg found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Winnipeg usually gets worse looks than most teams, and Vegas is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Not tonight: Winnipeg’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.2% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.1% (about 5.8% against Vegas) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Scheifele sets the Jets’ goals record
paras: It was a busy first period. Adam Lowry got the scoring started for the Jets just 29 seconds into the game. Brett Howden and Mitch Marner scored a minute and a half apart midway through the first to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Viggo Björck tied it up for Winnipeg late in the period. Tomáš Hertl put the Golden Knights back ahead 3-2 on the power play midway through the second. Mark Scheifele tied it up for Winnipeg less than five minutes later, and Kyle Connor put the Jets up 4-3 early in the third. Ivan Barbashev tied it 4-4 for Vegas with three and a half minutes left. William Karlsson scored the only goal of the shootout for the Golden Knights.

The Golden Knights had the better of the chances. Carter Hart made 26 saves for the Golden Knights, and Stuart Skinner stopped 29 of 33 at the other end. The Knights moved to 14-6-5, second in the Pacific, while the Jets dropped to 11-9-4, slipping to seventh in the Central.

items.text: Mark Scheifele passed Dale Hawerchuk to become the Jets’ all-time leader in goals, with 380.
Ivan Barbashev passed Chandler Stephenson for ninth on the Golden Knights’ all-time goals list, with 76.
The Golden Knights won for the first time in five games.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
